content: We simulate a routing scenario in which we send consecutive batches of the most difficult examples to the experts for annotation. We track changes in performance as we increase the number of most-difficult-articles sent to domain experts. As shown in Figure 4 , adding expert annotations for difficult articles consistently increases F1 scores. The performance gain is mostly from increased recall; the precision changes only a bit with higher quality annotation. This observation implies that crowd workers often fail to mark target tokens, but do not tend to produce large numbers of false positives. We suspect such failures to identify relevant spans/tokens are due to insufficient domain knowledge possessed by crowd workers.
